correctness.summary: Direct classification by the image of one bipartition class gives the exact standard and lazy counts. The range coefficients follow from diameter at most two and a two-family inclusion-exclusion for lazy range at most one. Strict discrete convexity proves the fixed-order extremizers. A standalone exhaustive verifier checks all 16 pairs with 1<=a,b<=4.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The full accessible HTML of Zhu's September 2026 source was inspected; it computes K_{2,3} as a running example but does not state a general complete-bipartite formula. Exact and synonymous searches found no equivalent range law or fixed-order extremal classification. The classical 2000 and 2003 source articles were not both completely inspected in full text, so an older unindexed special-case enumeration remains an explicit residual risk.

value.summary: The result upgrades the newest paper's isolated K_{2,3} calculations to full range distributions for every K_{a,b} in both models, identifies unique fixed-order extremizers, and exhibits a lazy-model asymptotic split from 1 for balanced bicliques to 2 for stars.

limitations: The formulas are specific to complete bipartite graphs and the uniform standard/lazy models.
The result does not resolve the stronger stochastic-domination form of the BHM conjecture.
The 2000 Benjamini-Haggstrom-Mossel and 2003 Loebl-Nesetril-Reed articles were not both completely inspected in full text; older unindexed coverage remains a concrete originality risk.
Finite computation supports but does not replace the proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
